<P
style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=center><B>PART I</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
1. </B></P>
<P
style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>DESCRIPTION
OF BUSINESS</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>History</U></B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>We were incorporated under the laws of the State of Idaho as
Superior Mines Company on January 22, 1962. &nbsp;We were established for the
purposes of mineral exploration in the state of Idaho and Montana. &nbsp;In 1964
our name was changed to Superior Silver Mines, Inc. &nbsp;The Company has been
dormant for a number of years. &nbsp;It currently holds one unpatented mineral
claim. &nbsp;There are no known mineral reserves on the Company&#146;s property.
&nbsp;Due to the increase in the price of gold, silver and other metals over the
past several years, management is reactivating the Company with the intention of
investigating opportunities in the natural resource industry. Because we have no
operations and only nominal assets we are what the Securities and Exchange
Commission &nbsp;defines as &nbsp;a shell company. At such time as we cease to
be a shell company we will need to file a Form 8-K that contains the information
that would be required in an initial registration statement on Form 10 or Form
10SB to register a class of securities under Section 12 of the Securities
Exchange Act of 1934. We will be required to file the Form 8-K within four
business days after the closing of the transaction that results in our no longer
being considered a shell company</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>We are registering its shares under the Securities Exchange Act of
1934 (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;) for the purpose of becoming a reporting company.
&nbsp;The Company believes that it will be better able to finance its operations
if it is a reporting company. &nbsp;Management believes the benefits of becoming
a reporting company include the ability to obtain support of market makers,
facilitating or improving the terms on which additional equity financing may be
sought, providing liquidity for stock options or similar benefits to key
employees, and providing liquidity for all shareholders by qualifying to list on
the NASDAQ supervised OTC Bulletin Board. </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>Risk
Factors</U></B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>The Company&#146;s business is subject to numerous risk factors,
including the following: </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Because the Company was historically engaged in the mineral
exploration industry, there exists the possibility that the Company may have
environmental liability. &nbsp;Management has no knowledge of any actions of the
Company that might give rise to such potential liability, but there can be no
assurance that the Company may not at some future date be deemed to have
environmental liabilities.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>The Company has had no revenues or earnings from operations. The
Company has no significant assets or financial resources. &nbsp;As a mineral
exploration company, the Company will sustain operating expenses without
corresponding revenues. &nbsp;This will result in the Company incurring net
operating losses that will increase continuously until the Company can bring a
property into production or lease, joint venture or sell any property it may
acquire.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Mineral exploration and development are highly speculative and
capital intensive. &nbsp;Most exploration efforts are not successful in that
they do not result in the discovery of mineralization of sufficient quantity or
quality to be profitably mined. &nbsp;The operations of the Company are also
indirectly subject to all of the hazards and risks normally incident to </P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>2</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>developing and operating mining properties. &nbsp;These risks
include insufficient ore reserves; fluctuations in production costs that may
make mining of reserves uneconomic; significant environmental and other
regulatory restrictions; labor disputes; geological problems; failure of pit
walls or dams; <I>force majeure</I> events; and the risk of injury to persons,
property or the environment.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Our property does not contain any reserves. The probability of an
individual prospect ever having reserves is remote. &nbsp;As such, any funds
spent on exploration could be lost which will result in a loss of your
investment. Even if we were ever to develop reserves, ore reserve figures and
costs are primarily estimates and are not guarantees of recovery of the
indicated quantities of these metals. &nbsp;There are numerous uncertainties
inherent in estimating proven and probable reserves and mineralization,
including many factors beyond the control of the Company. &nbsp;The estimation
of reserves and mineralization is a subjective process, and the accuracy of any
such estimates is a function of the quality of available data and of engineering
and geological interpretation and judgment. &nbsp;Results of drilling,
metallurgical testing and production and the evaluation of mine plans subsequent
to the date of any estimate may justify revision of such estimates. &nbsp;No
assurance can be given that the estimate of the amount of metal or the indicated
level of recovery of these metals will be realized. &nbsp;Reserve estimates for
properties that have not yet started production may change based on actual
production experience. &nbsp;Further, reserves are valued based on estimates of
costs and metals prices. &nbsp;The economic value of ore reserves may be
adversely affected by:</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>declines in the market price of the various metals we mine; </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>increased production or capital costs; or </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>recovery rates. </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Assumptions about prices are subject to greater uncertainty, and
metals prices have fluctuated widely in the past. &nbsp;Declines in the market
price of base or precious metals also may render reserves or mineralization
containing relatively lower grades of ore uneconomic to exploit. &nbsp;Changes
in operating and capital costs and other factors including, but not limited to,
short-term operating factors such as the need for sequential development of
orebodies and the processing of new or different ore grades may materially and
adversely affect reserves. &nbsp;However, if the price of metals declines
substantially below the levels used to calculate reserves for an extended
period, we could experience: </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>delays in new project development; </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>increased net losses; </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>reduced cash flow; </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>reductions in reserves; and </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>write-down of asset values.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>The profitability of mining operations is directly related to the
market price of the metals being mined. &nbsp;The market price of base and
precious metals such as copper, silver and gold fluctuate widely and is affected
by numerous factors beyond the control of any mining </P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>3</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>company. &nbsp;These factors include expectations with respect to
the rate of inflation, the exchange rates of the dollar and other currencies,
interest rates, global or regional political, economic or banking crises, and a
number of other factors. &nbsp;If the market price of silver or copper should
drop dramatically, the value of the Company&#146;s exploration properties could also
drop dramatically; and the Company might not be able to recover its investment
in those properties. &nbsp;The selection of a property for exploration or
development, the determination to construct a mine and place it into production,
and the dedication of funds necessary to achieve such purposes are decisions
that must be made long before the first revenues from production will be
received. &nbsp;Price fluctuations between the time that such decisions are made
and the commencement of production can drastically affect the economics of a
mine.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Our business is subject to extensive federal, state and local laws
and regulations governing development, production, labor standards, occupational
health, waste disposal, use of toxic substances, environmental regulations, mine
safety and other matters. &nbsp;New legislation and regulations may be adopted
at any time that results in additional operating expense, capital expenditures
or restrictions and delays in the mining, production or development of our
properties. &nbsp;Various laws and permits require that financial assurances be
in place for certain environmental and reclamation obligations and other
potential liabilities. &nbsp;The amount of the financial assurances and the
amount required to be set aside by us as collateral for these financial
assurances will be dependent upon a number of factors, including our financial
condition, reclamation cost estimates, development of new projects and the total
dollar value of financial assurances in place.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>We compete with other mineral exploration and mining companies,
almost all of which have greater financial resources than us or are further in
their development, for the acquisition of mineral claims, leases and other
mineral interests as well as for the recruitment and retention of qualified
employees and other personnel. &nbsp;If we require and are unsuccessful in
acquiring additional mineral properties or personnel, we will not be able to
grow at the rate we desire, or at all.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>You should not rely on an investment in our common stock to
provide dividend income, as we do not plan to pay cash dividends on our common
stock in the foreseeable future. </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Our common stock is quoted on the Pink Sheets. &nbsp;Trading in
stock quoted in the Pink Sheets is often thin and characterized by wide
fluctuations in trading prices due to many factors that may have little to do
with our operations or business prospects. &nbsp;This volatility could depress
the market price of our common stock for reasons unrelated to operating
performance. &nbsp;Moreover, the Pink Sheets is not a stock exchange, and
trading of securities on the Pink Sheets is often more sporadic than the trading
of securities listed on a quotation system or a stock exchange such as the Amex.
&nbsp;Accordingly, shareholders may have difficulty reselling any of the
shares.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>One of our directors, Terrence Dunne served as the Chief Financial
Officer and a Director for Daybreak Oil and Gas, Inc. (Daybreak) from April 2006
until December , 2007. During Mr. Dunne&#146;s tenure with Daybreak, the Company
experienced two delinquent filings. The Form 10-QSB for the fiscal quarter ended
November 30, 2006 and the Form 10-KSB for the fiscal year ended February 28,
2007 were filed subsequent to their statutory due dates.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>4</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>The filings were delinquent due to management&#146;s decision (which
included Mr. Dunne) to restate previously filed financial statements. The
restated financial statements included the four (4) quarters for the fiscal year
ended February 28, 2006 and the first three (3) quarters for the fiscal year
ended February 28, 2007. The decision to restate these financial periods was in
response to comments of the SEC staff in connection with the submission of a
registration statement. These comments involved the Commission&#146;s interpretation
of recently enacted accounting standards concerning the valuation of stock based
compensation. The decision to restate the financial statements was predicated on
the pre-effective application of newly enacted accounting standards. The
Company's management conferred with the Company's audit committee and the
Company's independent public accounting firm to arrive at this decision </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Our stock is a penny stock. &nbsp;The Securities and Exchange
Commission has adopted Rule 15g-9 which generally defines &#147;penny stock&#148; to be
any equity security that has a market price (as defined) less than $5.00 per
share or an exercise price of less than $5.00 per share, subject to certain
exceptions. &nbsp;Our securities are covered by the penny stock rules which
impose additional sales practice requirements on broker-dealers who sell to
persons other than established customers and &#147;accredited investors.&#148; &nbsp;The
term &#147;accredited investor&#148; refers generally to institutions with assets in
excess of $5,000,000 or individuals with a net worth in excess of $1,000,000 or
annual income exceeding $200,000 individually or $300,000 jointly with their
spouse. &nbsp;The penny stock rules require a broker-dealer, prior to a
transaction in a penny stock not otherwise exempt from the rules, to deliver a
standardized risk disclosure document in a form prepared by the SEC which
provides information about penny stocks and the nature and level of risks in the
penny stock market. &nbsp;The broker-dealer also must provide the customer with
current bid and offer quotations for the penny stock, the compensation of the
broker-dealer and its salesperson in the transaction, and monthly account
statements showing the market value of each penny stock held in the customer&#146;s
account. &nbsp;The bid and offer quotations and the broker-dealer and
salesperson compensation information must be given to the customer orally or in
writing prior to effecting the transaction and must be given to the customer in
writing before or with the customer&#146;s confirmation. &nbsp;In addition, the penny
stock rules require that, prior to a transaction in a penny stock not otherwise
exempt from these rules, the broker-dealer must make a special written
determination that the penny stock is a suitable investment for the purchaser
and receive the purchaser&#146;s written agreement to the transaction. &nbsp;These
disclosure requirements may have the effect of reducing the level of trading
activity in the secondary market for the stock that is subject to these penny
stock rules. &nbsp;Consequently, these penny stock rules may affect the ability
of broker-dealers to trade our securities. &nbsp;We believe that the penny stock
rules discourage investor interest in and limit the marketability of our common
stock.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>In addition to the &#147;penny stock&#148; rules promulgated by the
Securities and Exchange Commission, the NASD has adopted rules that require, in
recommending an investment to a customer, a broker-dealer must have reasonable
grounds for believing that the investment is suitable for that customer.
&nbsp;Prior to recommending speculative, low-priced securities to their
non-institutional customers, broker-dealers must make reasonable efforts to
obtain information about the customer&#146;s financial status, tax status, investment
objectives and other information. &nbsp;Under interpretations of these rules,
the NASD believes there is a high probability that speculative, low-priced
securities will not be suitable for at least some customers. &nbsp;The NASD
requirements make it more difficult for broker-dealers to recommend </P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>5</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>that their customers buy our common stock, which may limit your
ability to buy and sell our stock. </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>Employees</U></B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>We currently have no employees. &nbsp;We intend to utilize the
services of outside consultants and contractors to provide additional services
to the Company.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>Competition</U></B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>There is aggressive competition within the minerals industry to
discover and acquire properties considered to have commercial potential.
&nbsp;The Company competes for the opportunity to participate in promising
exploration projects with other entities, many of which have greater resources
than the Company. &nbsp;In addition, the Company competes with others in efforts
to obtain financing to explore and develop mineral properties.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>Regulation</U></B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>The Company&#146;s activities in the United States are subject to
various federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing prospecting,
development, production, labor standards, occupational health and mine safety,
control of toxic substances, and other matters involving environmental
protection and taxation. &nbsp;It is possible that future changes in these laws
or regulations could have a significant impact on the Company&#146;s business,
causing those activities to be economically reevaluated at that time.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
2.</B></P>
<P
style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>MANAGEMENT&#146;S
DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OR PLAN OF OPERATION</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>Plan
of Operation</U></B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>The Company is voluntarily registering its common stock under the
Securities Exchange Act of 1934. &nbsp;After completion of this registration, it
is the Company&#146;s intention to obtain a listing on the NASDAQ Supervised OTC
Bulletin Board. &nbsp;The Company believes that listing on the OTCBB will
facilitate the Company&#146;s efforts to obtain additional equity financing.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>The Company does not anticipate a significant change in the number
of employees during the next 12 months. &nbsp;The Company intends to rely upon
the use of outside consultants to provide services to the Company. &nbsp;These
plans could change depending upon the timing and nature of any acquisitions of
mineral exploration properties (none of which are under consideration at this
time). &nbsp;During the next 12 months, the Company expects to be able to
satisfy its cash requirements. &nbsp;The Company does not foresee the need to
raise additional capital during this period.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 6px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B><I>Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</I></B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 6px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>There are no preliminary agreements or understandings between the
Company and its officers and directors or affiliates or lending institutions
with respect to any loan agreements. </P>

<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>Board
Committees</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>The entire Board of Directors presently serves as our Audit,
Nominating and Compensation Committees and will continue to serve in such
capacity until said committees are established. &nbsp;We have not yet adopted a
Code of Ethics for our Executive Officers but intend to do so during the second
quarter of 2008.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>Conflicts
of Interest</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Officers and Directors have a fiduciary duty to our shareholders
and owe the Company a duty to advance the Company&#146;s business interests when the
opportunity to do so arises. As a result, Officers and Directors are prohibited
from taking personal advantage of certain business opportunities in which the
Company may be interested. This so-called &#147;corporate opportunity doctrine&#148; is
complicated and it is not possible to clearly define all of the business
opportunities which belong or could be of interest to the Company and what
business opportunities may be taken advantage of personally by Officers or
Directors. The most common types of situations falling within this corporate
opportunity doctrine prohibit Officers and Directors from: (i) personally taking
advantage of any business opportunity that typically would be pursued by, or
would be of interest to, the Company; (ii) personally taking advantage of any
other business opportunity that the Company may want to take advantage of if the
opportunity is discovered using Company property, business contacts or
information, or that the Officer becomes aware of because he or she works for
the Company (or that a Director becomes aware of in his or her capacity as a
director of the Company).</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>Legal
Proceedings</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>No Director, or person nominated to become a Director or Executive
Officer, has been involved in any legal action involving the Company during the
past five years.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
6.</B></P>

style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>EXECUTIVE
COMPENSATION</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 13px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>None of our officers or directors receive any compensation for
serving in such position. In &nbsp;June 2007 we authorized the payment of
224,000 shares of our common stock to the Thomas S. Smith. This compensation
represented compensation for legal services performed by Mr. Smith over the
previous seven years. The shares were valued at $0.025 per share based upon
management&#146;s estimate of the fair value of the shares on the date of
issuance.</P>

<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
8.</B></P>
<P
style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>DESCRIPTION
OF SECURITIES</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>COMMON
STOCK</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>We are authorized to issue five hundred million (500,000,000)
shares of $0.0001 par value common stock. &nbsp;All of the common stock
authorized has equal voting rights and powers without restrictions in
preference. &nbsp;All shares of common stock are equal to each other with
respect to voting, liquidation, dividend and other rights. &nbsp;Owners of
shares of common stock are entitled to one vote for each share of common stock
owned at any shareholders&#146; meeting. &nbsp;Holders of shares of common stock are
entitled to receive such dividends as may be declared by the Board of Directors
out of funds legally available therefor; and upon liquidation, are entitled to
participate pro rata in a distribution of assets available for such a
distribution to shareholders.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>At March 18, 2008, there were 20,654,398 shares of common stock
issued and outstanding held by approximately 1,392 shareholders of record.
&nbsp;There are no outstanding options. </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>PREFERRED
STOCK</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>We are authorized to issue 10,000,000 shares of Preferred Stock.
At December 11, 2007, there were no shares of preferred stock issued and
outstanding. &nbsp;The Preferred Stock is entitled to preference over the Common
Stock with respect to the distribution of assets of the Company in the event of
liquidation, dissolution, or winding-up of the Company, whether voluntarily or
involuntarily, or in the event of any other distribution of assets of the
Company among its shareholders for the purpose of winding-up its affairs.
&nbsp;The authorized but un-issued shares of Preferred Stock may be divided into
and issued in designated series from time to time by one or more resolutions
adopted by the Board of Directors. &nbsp;The Directors in their sole discretion
have the power to determine the preferences, limitations, and relative rights of
each series of Preferred Stock within the limits set forth in the Idaho Business
Corporations Act. &nbsp;As of the date of this memorandum, no preferred stock
has been issued.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>There are no conversion, preemptive, or other subscription rights
or privileges with respect to any shares. &nbsp;Our stock does not have
cumulative voting rights, which means that the holders of more than fifty
percent (50%) of the shares voting in an election of directors may elect all of
the directors if they choose to do so. &nbsp;In such event, the holders of the
remaining shares aggregating less than fifty percent (50%) would not be able to
elect any directors.</P>

style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Transfer Agent</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>We utilize the services of Columbia Stock Transfer Company, 601
East Seltice Way, Suite 202, Post Falls, Idaho 83854, as our transfer agent and
registrar. </P>

interim period, the principal accountant had not resigned (or declined to stand
for re-election) or was dismissed.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>11</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>In addition, the Company&#146;s principal accountant had no
disagreements with the Company on any matter of Financial Reporting Policies and
Procedures.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
4.</B></P>
<P
style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>RECENT
SALES OF UNREGISTERED SECURITIES</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>During
December 2006, the Company sold 552,000 shares of its unregistered common stock
for $0.025 per share. &nbsp;The proceeds to the Company from the sale were
$13,800. &nbsp;The shares were offered to and purchased by four individuals,
each of whom was an accredited investor. The purchasers consisted of three
directors and one executive officer of the Company. Management believes that the
offering was exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933 (&#147;the
Act&#146;) pursuant to Rule 506 of Regulation D and Section 4(2) of the Act.
&nbsp;Proceeds from the offering were used to fund the Company&#146;s general and
administrative expenses. All offers were made by the issued and no commissions
were paid, directly or indirectly, &nbsp;in connection with the offer and sale
of the shares.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>During
July and August 2007, the Company sold 10,325,000 shares of its unregistered
common stock for $0.04 per share. &nbsp;The shares were offered and sold only to
accredited investors as that term is defined in Regulation D. Commissions of
$41,300 were paid to underwriters in connection with the offering. These shares
were issued on September 13, 2007 and the proceeds to the Company from the
offering were $360,085. the names of the purchasers and the number of shares
acquired and the dollar amount invested are set forth as follows:</P>

be used to fund the Company&#146;s general and administrative expenses.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>During
October 2007, the Company sold 516,250 shares of its unregistered common stock
for $0.08 per share. &nbsp;This sale related to the exercise of all of the
warrants received by the Placement Agent in the July and August 2007 private
placement. &nbsp;The proceeds to the Company from the exercise were $41,300.
Proceeds from the exercise are expected to be used to fund the Company&#146;s general
and administrative expenses. Management believes that the sales were exempt from
registration under the Securities Act of 1933 (&#147;the Act&#146;) pursuant to Section
4(2) of the Act.</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>13</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>ITEM 5.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>INDEMNIFICATION OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Although the Company&#146;s Articles of Incorporation and By Laws do
not address the subject of indemnification, The Idaho Business Corporations Act
Sections 30-1-850 through 30-1-859, permits the Company to indemnify its
officers and directors against liabilities they incur in such positions.
Pursuant to the Idaho Business Corporations Act, both permissible and mandatory
indemnification is provided for officers and directors of the Company. </P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.3pt"
align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 93px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -93px; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.3pt"
align=justify><U>Permissive Indemnification</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 93px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(1)</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 93px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.3pt"
align=justify>Except as otherwise provided by law, a corporation may indemnify
an individual who is a party to any threatened, pending or completed action,
suit or proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative, arbitrative or
investigative and whether formal or informal (a &#147;Proceeding&#148;) because he is a
director against liability incurred in the proceeding if:</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(a) &nbsp;</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(i) &nbsp;</P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>He conducted himself in good faith; and</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(ii) &nbsp;</P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>He reasonably believed:</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 192px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(A) &nbsp;</P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 192px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>In the case of conduct in his official capacity, that his</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 240px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>conduct was in the best interest of the corporation, and </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 240px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(B)</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 240px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>In all cases, that his conduct was at least not opposed to the
best interests of the corporation; and</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 192px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(iii)</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 192px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>In the case of any criminal proceeding, he had no reasonable cause
to believe his conduct was unlawful; or</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 144px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(b)</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 144px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>He engaged in conduct for which broader indemnification has been
made permissible or obligatory under a provision of the articles of
incorporation, as authorized by section 30-1-202(2)(e), Idaho Code.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(2)</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>A director's conduct with respect to an employee plan for a
purpose he reasonably believed to be in the best interests of the participants
in, and the beneficiaries of, the plan is conduct that satisfies the requirement
of subsection (1)(a)(ii)(B) above.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(3)</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>The termination of a proceeding by judgment, order, settlement or
conviction, or upon a plea of nolo contendere or its equivalent, is not, of
itself, determinative that the director did not meet the relevant standard of
conduct described in this section.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(4)</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Unless ordered by a court under section 30-1-854(1)(c), Idaho
Code, a corporation may not indemnify a director:</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 144px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(a)</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 144px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>In connection with a proceeding by or in the right of the
corporation, except for reasonable expenses incurred in connection with the
proceeding if it is determined that the director has met the relevant standard
of conduct under subsection (1) of this section; or</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 144px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>(b)</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 144px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>In connection with any proceeding with respect to conduct for
which he was adjudged liable on the basis that he received a financial benefit
to which he was not entitled, whether or not involving action in his official
capacity.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Mandatory Indemnification</U> &nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 13.3pt" align=justify>A
corporation shall indemnify a director who was wholly successful, on the merits
or otherwise, in the defense of any proceeding to which he was a party because
he was a director of the corporation against reasonable expenses incurred by him
in connection with the proceeding.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>14</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -96px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Public Policy</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>Insofar
as indemnification for liabilities arising under the Securities Act of 1933 (the
"Act") may be permitted to directors, officers and controlling persons of the
small business issuer pursuant to the foregoing provisions, or otherwise, the
small business issuer has been advised that in the opinion of the Securities and
Exchange Commission such indemnification is against public policy as expressed
in the Act and is, therefore, unenforceable.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 14px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=center><BR><BR></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>To the Board of Directors and</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Stockholders of Superior Silver Mines, Inc.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-RIGHT: 76px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>We have audited the accompanying balance sheets of Superior Silver
Mines, Inc., (An Exploration Stage Company) (&#147;the Company&#148;) as of December 31,
2007 and 2006, and the related statements of operations, changes in
stockholders&#146; equity and cash flows for the years then ended and for the period
of exploration stage (January 1, 2007) through December 31, 2007. These
financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our
responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on
our audits.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-RIGHT: 76px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the
Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards
require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about
whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit
includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and
disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the
accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well
as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our
audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-RIGHT: 76px; PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>In our opinion, the financial statements referred to above present
fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of Superior Silver
Mines, Inc. as of December 31, 2007 and 2006, and the results of its operations
and its cash flows for the years then ended and for the period of exploration
stage (January 1, 2007) through December 31, 2007 in conformity with accounting
principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>21</P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"><B>Superior Silver
Mines, Inc.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"><I>(An Exploration
Stage Company)</I></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"><B>Notes to Financial
Statements</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>1.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Description of Business</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
Company was incorporated under the laws of the State of Idaho as Superior Mines
Company on January 22, 1962. &nbsp;The Company was established for the purposes
of mineral exploration in the states of Idaho and Montana. &nbsp;In 1964, the
Company&#146;s name was changed to Superior Silver Mines, Inc. &nbsp;The Company has
been dormant for a number of years. &nbsp;It currently holds one unpatented
mineral claim. &nbsp;There are no known mineral reserves on the Company&#146;s
property. &nbsp;Due to the increase in the price of gold, silver and other
metals over the past several years, management is reactivating the Company with
the intention of investigating opportunities in the natural resource
industry.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
Company is an exploration stage company and has incurred losses since the period
of exploration stage (January 1, 2007). &nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>2.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Exploration Stage Enterprise</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
Company&#146;s financial statements are prepared in accordance with the provisions of
Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 7, &#147;Accounting for Development
Stage Enterprises,&#148; as it devotes substantially all its efforts to exploring for
mining interests and developing opportunities that will eventually provide
sufficient net profits to sustain the Company&#146;s existence. &nbsp;Until such
interests and opportunities are engaged in commercial production, the Company
will continue to prepare its financial statements in accordance with entities in
the exploration stage.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify><U>Cash
and Cash Equivalents</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>For the
purpose of the balance sheet and statement of cash flows, the Company considers
all highly liquid investments purchased, with an original maturity of three
months or less, to be cash equivalent.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify><U>Fair
Value of Financial Instruments</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
carrying amounts of financial instruments, including cash and cash equivalents
and accounts payable, approximated their fair values at December 31, 2007 and
2006. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Exploration Costs</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Exploration costs are expensed in the period in which they occur.
&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>22</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"><B>Superior Silver
Mines, Inc.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"><I>(An Exploration
Stage Company)</I></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"><B>Notes to Financial
Statements</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>2.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, continued:</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify><U>Use
of Estimates</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles
generally accepted in the United States of America requires management to make
estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial
statements and accompanying notes. &nbsp;Actual results could differ from those
estimates.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify><U>Net
Loss Per Share</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>Such
amounts, representing basic and diluted loss per share, are computed based on
the weighted average number of shares outstanding during the periods December
31, 2007 and 2006.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Income Taxes</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>Income
taxes are recognized in accordance with Statement of Financial Accounting
Standards No. 109, &#147;Accounting for Income Taxes,&#148; whereby deferred income tax
liabilities or assets at the end of each period are determined using the tax
rate expected to be in effect when the taxes are actually paid or recovered.
&nbsp;A valuation allowance is recognized on deferred tax assets when it is more
likely than not that some or all of these deferred tax assets will not be
realized. &nbsp;The Company has not recorded an income tax provision, as it has
no taxable income. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>In June
2006, the FASB issued Interpretation No. 48, &#147;Accounting for Uncertainty in
Income Taxes &#150; an interpretation of FASB Statement No. 109&#148; (hereinafter "FIN
48"), which prescribes a recognition threshold and measurement attribute for the
financial statement recognition and measurement of a tax position taken or
expected to be taken in a tax return. FIN 48 also provides guidance on
de-recognition, classification, interest and penalties, accounting in interim
periods, disclosure and transition. The Company adopted FIN 48 on January 1,
2007. &nbsp;It&#146;s adoption had no effect on the Company&#146;s financial position or
results of operations. </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>23</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>

<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>2.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, continued:</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Stock Based Compensation</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>In
December 2004, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued SFAS No.
123(R), &#147;Share-Based Payment.&#148; &nbsp;This Statement is a revision to SFAS No.
123, &#147;Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation,&#148; and supersedes APB Opinion No.
25, &#147;Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees&#148; under which guidance the
intrinsic value method was prescribed for awards to employees for services. SFAS
No. 123(R) requires the measurement of the cost of employee services received in
exchange for an award of equity instruments based on the grant-date fair value
of the award. The cost will be recognized over the period during which an
employee is required to provide service in exchange for the award. No
compensation cost is recognized for equity instruments for which employees do
not render service.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
Company adopted SFAS No. 123(R) using the modified prospective transition
method, which requires the application of the accounting standard as of January
1, 2006. There was no impact on the financial statements as of and for the year
ended December 31, 2006 as a result of the adoption of SFAS No. 123(R). In
accordance with the modified prospective transition method, the financial
statements for prior periods have not been restated to reflect, and do not
include, the impact of SFAS No. 123(R).</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Reclamation and Remediation</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
Company&#146;s properties have been and are subject to, standards for mine
reclamation that have been established by various governmental agencies.
&nbsp;In June&nbsp;2001, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;)
issued SFAS No. 143, &#147;Accounting for Asset Retirement Obligations&#148;.&nbsp; SFAS
143 requires the Company to record the fair value of an asset retirement
obligation as a liability in the period in which the Company incurs a legal
obligation for the retirement of tangible long-lived assets.&nbsp; A
corresponding asset is also recorded and depreciated over the life of the
asset.&nbsp; After the initial measurement of the asset retirement obligation,
the liability will be adjusted at the end of each reporting period to reflect
changes in the estimated future cash flows underlying the obligation.&nbsp;
Determination of any amounts recognized upon adoption is based upon numerous
estimates and assumptions, including future retirement costs, future inflation
rates and the credit-adjusted risk-free interest rates. </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Environmental costs relating to properties put into production
will be estimated based primarily upon environmental and regulatory
requirements, and are accrued and charged to expense over the expected economic
life of the operation using the units-of-production method. &nbsp;The liability
for reclamation is classified as current or long-term based on the expected
timing of the expenditures.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>

align=justify><B>2.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, continued:</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
Company accrues costs associated with environmental remediation obligations when
it is probable that such costs will be incurred and they are reasonably
estimable. &nbsp;Such costs will be based on management&#146;s estimate of amounts
expected to be incurred when remediation work is performed. &nbsp;To date,
management is unaware of any environmental proceedings or action pending against
the Company.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>In
September 2006, the FASB issued Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No.
157, &#147;Fair Value Measurements,&#148; (hereinafter "SFAS No. 157") which defines fair
value, establishes a framework for measuring fair value in generally accepted
accounting principles (GAAP), and expands disclosures about fair value
measurements. Where applicable, SFAS No. 157 simplifies and codifies related
guidance within GAAP and does not require any new fair value measurements. SFAS
No. 157 is effective for financial statements issued for fiscal years beginning
after November 15, 2007, and interim periods within those fiscal years. Earlier
adoption is encouraged. The Company does not expect the adoption of SFAS No. 157
to have a significant immediate effect on its financial position or results of
operation.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>In
December 2007, the FASB issued SFAS No. 160, &#147;Noncontrolling Interests in
Consolidated Financial Statements &#150; an amendment of ARB 51,&#148; which is effective
for fiscal years and interim periods within those fiscal years, beginning on or
after December 15, 2008. &nbsp;SFAS No. 160 amends ARB 51 to establish
accounting and reporting standards for the noncontrolling ownership interest in
a subsidiary and for the deconsolidation of a subsidiary. &nbsp;We are currently
evaluating the potential impact of this statement on our financial statements
and at this time we do not anticipate a material effect.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>In
December 2007, the FASB revised SFAS No. 141 &#147;Business Combinations.&#148; &nbsp;The
revised standard is effective for transactions where the acquisition date is on
or after the beginning of the first annual reporting period beginning on or
after December 15, 2008. &nbsp;SFAS No. 141(R) will change the accounting for
the assets acquired and liabilities assumed in a business combination.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Acquisition costs will be generally expenses as incurred;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Noncontrolling interests (formally known as &#147;minority interests&#148;)
will be valued at fair value at the acquisition date;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify>Acquired contingent liabilities will be recorded at fair value at
the acquisition date and subsequently measured at either the higher of such
amount or the amount determined under existing guidance for nonacquired
contingencies;</P>

Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities,&#148; which permits entities to choose to
measure many financial assets and financial liabilities at fair value.
&nbsp;Unrealized gains on items for which the fair value option has been elected
are to be reported in earnings. &nbsp;SFAS No. 159 will become effective as of
the beginning of the first fiscal year that begins after November 15, 2007.
&nbsp;We do not anticipate the adoption of SFAS No. 159 to have a material
effect on our results of operations or financial position.</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"><B>3.</B></P>
<P
style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"><B>Income
Taxes</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
Company did not record an income tax provision for the years ended December 31,
2007 and 2006, as it had no taxable income. At December 31, 2007 and 2006, the
Company had net operating loss carryforwards available for income tax purposes
of approximately $732,000 and $687,000, respectively, which will expire in
various amounts from 2008 through 2027. &nbsp;The associated deferred tax asset
at December 31, 2007 and 2006 is approximately $293,000 and $275,000,
respectively, which was calculated assuming a 40% marginal combined federal and
state income tax rate, and has been fully reserved as management believes it is
more likely than not that the deferred tax asset will not be utilized. &nbsp;In
accordance with Internal Revenue Code Section 382, pre-2007 net operating loss
carryovers will be limited to approximately $32,000 per year due to the
significant ownership change during the year ended December 31, 2007.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>The
following is a reconciliation of the reported amount of income tax expense
attributable to continuing operations for the years ended December 31, 2007 and
2006, to the amount of income tax expense that would result from applying
domestic federal statutory tax rates to pretax income from continuing
operations:</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>

<P

align=justify><B>4.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Stockholders&#146; Equity</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Common Stock</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>At
December 31, 2006, the Company was authorized to issue up to 10,000,000 shares
of its $0.10 par value common stock. &nbsp;At December 31, 2006, the Company had
one class of common stock authorized, issued and outstanding.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>During
2007, the Company&#146;s shareholders approved a change in the authorized common
stock of the Company from 10,000,000 shares of $0.10 par value common stock to
500,000,000 shares of $0.0001 par value common stock. &nbsp;The shareholders
also approved the authorization of 10,000,000 shares of $0.0001 par value
preferred stock.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>27</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Superior Silver Mines, Inc.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify><I>(An
Exploration Stage Company)</I></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Notes to Financial Statements</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>4.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Stockholders&#146; Equity, continued:</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Private Placement</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>During
December 2006, the Company sold 552,000 shares of its unregistered common stock
for $0.025 per share. &nbsp;The proceeds to the Company from the sale were
$13,800. &nbsp;Proceeds from the offering are expected to be used to fund the
Company&#146;s general and administrative expenses.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>During
July and August 2007, the Company sold 10,325,000 shares of its unregistered
common stock for $0.04 per share. &nbsp;These shares were issued on September
13, 2007 and the proceeds to the Company from the offering were $360,085.
&nbsp;Proceeds from the offering are expected to be used to fund the Company&#146;s
general and administrative expenses.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>During
October 2007, the Company issued 516,250 shares of its unregistered common stock
in connection with the exercise of warrants at $0.08 per share. &nbsp;The
warrants were granted to a placement agent as compensation for the July and
August 2007 private placement. &nbsp;The proceeds to the Company from the
exercise were $41,300, and are expected to be used to fund the Company&#146;s general
and administrative expenses.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><U>Common Stock Issued for Management and Consulting
Services</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>On June
27, 2006, the Company issued 224,000 shares to Thomas S. Smith, the Company&#146;s
President, and 224,000 shares to H.F. Magnuson, father of a director of the
Company, for services rendered to the Company. The shares were valued at $0.025
per share based upon management&#146;s estimate of their fair value at the date of
issuance.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: -18px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>5.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: 48px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify><B>Related Party Transactions</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify>In
addition to the related party transactions described in Note 4, at December 31,
2007 and 2006, the Company owed H.F. Magnuson &amp; Company, a company
controlled by H.F. Magnuson, father of a Director of the Company, $6,570 and
$289, respectively for office expenses. &nbsp;During 2007, the Company paid H.F.
Magnuson &amp; Company $2,026 for office expenses.</P>
